title: Real-Time Markerless Motion Capture for Interactive Applications and Game Engines: Pipelines, Spatio-Temporal Refinement, and Latency Budgets
content: The rapid evolution of deep learning and computer vision has moved markerless mo-tion capture (MoCap) from specialized biomechanical tools into a key technology for real-time interactive systems, video game engines, and virtual production. This review analyzes state-of-the-art markerless pipelines and focuses on integrating 3D human pose estimation (HPE) into standard graphics engines. We evaluate the shift from sin-gle-view regression to temporal convolutional architectures. Our review emphasizes the trade-offs between spatial precision and algorithmic overhead for interactive use cases. Central to our analysis is the spatio-temporal refinement of noisy skeletal data. We assess adaptive smoothing techniques, such as the 1-Euro filter and predictive neural filtering, designed to minimize jitter and motion-to-photon latency. Findings indicate that modern markerless systems approach the standards of marker-based tools. However, maintaining temporal consistency under strict real-time budgets re-mains a fundamental challenge for human-display feedback loops. We examine indus-try-standard engines and their role in permitting seamless character retargeting throughout diverse applications, including clinical monitoring and sports coaching. Ultimately, this work synthesizes methodologies to optimize the responsiveness of AI-based MoCap systems within contemporary real-time software architectures.
